t: Paragraph (13) of section 101 of the Act entitled “An Act to provide for increases in appropriation ceilings and boundary changes in certain units of the National Park System, and for other purposes”, approved October 21, 1976 (90 Stat. 2732, 2733), is amended by changing the period to a semicolon and inserting the following thereafter: “the Secretary of the Interior is authorized to revise the boundary of the seashore to add approximately two hundred and seventy-four acres and to delete approximately two thousand acres, and sections 302 and 303 of the Act of April 11, 1972 (86 Stat 120, 121), shall apply to the boundary revision authorized herein.”.

fable.w: The section authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to revise a national seashore boundary and applies two cross-referenced provisions of a 1972 Act. The tempting reading is that a boundary revision implies public notice, rulemaking, or consultation with local interests, but the text names no outside party, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The cross-referenced sections are not reproduced here, so nothing in the text shows a non-federal party taking part in the decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Interior is authorized to revise the boundary of the seashore to add approximately two hundred and seventy-four acres and to delete approximately two thousand acres

opus.w: The section only authorizes a federal official, the Secretary of the Interior, to revise a National Seashore boundary. It does not require consultation with states, local governments or the public, and it sets up no advisory body, comment period, hearing or right to sue. The cross-reference to sections 302 and 303 of the 1972 Act doesn't say what those sections require. Assuming they add outside participation would mean reading in something this text doesn't show.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Interior is authorized to revise the boundary of the seashore to add approximately two hundred and seventy-four acres and to delete approximately two thousand acres
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section cross-references "sections 302 and 303 of the Act of April 11, 1972," which might set out boundary-revision procedures. Those could involve notice or consultation. But the text of the referenced sections isn't in front of me. On its face, this section only gives the Secretary of the Interior authority to change the seashore's boundary. It names no outside party, and it requires no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or consultation.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to revise boundaries and states that other statutory sections apply. It does not explicitly describe or mandate any consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties within its own text. The reference to other sections is a cross-reference, not a direct requirement of participation in this specific provision.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Interior is authorized to revise the boundary of the seashore to add approximately two hundred and seventy-four acres and to delete approximately two thousand acres, and sections 302 and 303 of the Act of April 11, 1972 (86 Stat 120, 121), shall apply to the boundary revision authorized herein.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "sections 302 and 303 of the Act of April 11, 1972," and those sections might contain participation requirements (like public hearings), this section implicitly requires participation. However, the definition requires us to look at what *this* section recommends or requires. This section itself only authorizes the Secretary to revise boundaries and states that other statutory provisions apply. It does not explicitly mandate a specific participatory process within its own text. More importantly, even if it did, the primary action is an administrative boundary revision by a federal official. Without explicit language in *this* section requiring consultation with outsiders, public comment, or advisory boards, it is safer to label it "No". The reference to other sections is a cross-reference, not a direct mandate of participation in this specific text block.

Actually, looking closer at the definition: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." This section authorizes the Secretary to revise boundaries. It says "sections 302 and 303... shall apply". If those sections require participation, does this section "recommend or require" it? The prompt asks if *this section* recommends or requires it. Usually, if a section just says "X applies," and X is not defined here, we look at the text provided. The text provided does not describe any participation mechanism. It describes an authorization for the Secretary to act. The "participation" is not in this text. Therefore, "No".
